2028 Lexus RX Mid-Cycle Refresh Debuts Virtually, Featuring Both Styling and Technical Updates
22 photos
Photo: TopElectricSUV.com
The premium Japanese automaker Lexus has been pretty busy with its collection of 2027 model year changes and updates: they put a price tag on the 2027 RZ in the States, gave the 2027 NX multiple upgrades and a touch of Mars, and the family-oriented TX bid farewell to the slow-selling and expensive 550h+ plug-in hybrid, leaving the rest of the range to get the latest upgrades.
How about the most popular Lexus RX ? Well, following the facelift of the second-gen NX, Lexus is reportedly working around the clock on the next big thing – the mid-cycle refresh for the fifth-gen RX, which has been around since the spring of 2022 and is being tested for its facelift, as per our spy photographer partners.
Well, the rumor mill also wants to contribute, and the good folks from the " TopElectricSUV " news outlet have some thoughts about the BMW X5 Neue Klasse rival, along with illustrations thanks to their member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to aid their cause.
In terms of design, Lexus is not expected to implement major changes – just cosmetic revisions like restyled headlamp graphics and a fresh bumper at the front along with a reworked ‘spindle body’ grille. New alloy wheels might also arrive, and there’s also a potential refresh of the rear with new taillight graphics and minor adjustments to the bumper.
On the other hand, bigger changes might arrive inside, where Lexus is rumored to switch to a slimmer and less cluttered dashboard for a cleaner look – it could follow the guidelines of the all-new ES with a separate 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and a free-standing 14-inch infotainment screen.
It could still have touch-operated climate controls, but the software and processing power could be newer and more efficient. Last but not least, a new steering wheel might also arrive. Currently, Lexus offers three powertrains for the RX, all electrified: 246 hp hybrid (RX 350h), the 366-hp for the 500h, and 304 hp for the 450h+ plug-in hybrid.
However, the facelift might bring the sixth-generation Lexus hybrid technology for both HEV and PHEV applications, with improved fuel efficiency thanks to the use of silicon-carbide (SiC) semiconductors and lower overall weight.
The plug-in hybrid model could see larger changes – a bigger 22.7 kWh battery pack for additional EV range along with a slight power bump that could match the 324 combined hp offered by the latest RAV4 PHEV. Charging could also become faster with support for 50 kW DC at fast-charging stations. So, what do you think about these proposed changes? Will they make the RX a worthier opponent for the likes of the Volvo XC60, the Neue Klasse BMW X5, and the recently facelifted Mercedes GLE?
